description: shared-residence agreement now gates MUA/BUA/actual/telephone outcomes (adversarial case returns $0)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The MUA dollar output was computed directly from page-163's ungated `household_entitled_to_mandatory_utility_allowance`, so it paid the mandatory utility allowance even when multiple households sharing one residence had not agreed on an allowance type, which SNAP Manual p.165 requires.
triage.triage_notes: Two-module fix; this module carries the propagation half. The only semantic change is in `sc_current_snap_standard_utility_allowance_state_value`: the import target and formula reference move from `us-sc:policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-163#household_entitled_to_mandatory_utility_allowance` to `us-sc:policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-165#multiple_utility_allowance_entitlement`. Pre-fix those two were semantically identical (p.165's MUA rule was a pass-through), so the re-route only bites once index 1 adds the agreement conjunct — i.e. this is the change that carries the missing p.165 clause into the money output. The other two hunks (limited/individual allowance rules) are import-hash bumps only (15aefb4d -> 9146cdfb) from page-165 changing: mechanical bookkeeping riding along with the real change. Provision read via resolve_provision.py against release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (fix_time_corpus_match: same_body); p.165 text confirms the agreement requirement. Companion test page-159.test.yaml adds `shared_residence_disagreement_blocks_mua_assignment` / `..._bua_assignment` cases asserting $0. Quote is from a maintainer comment on PR #1139 recording the repair round (stored as an issue_comment, not a formal review object); commit body is empty and the subject is 'fix: require shared-residence utility agreement'. Related but separate findings in the same review round (page-369 $33 vs $27 collision, uncited rent exclusion, p.163 timing qualifications) were fixed in other commits, not this one.
triage.verifier_justification: The attempted refutation fails: module 0's diff changes encoded meaning, not just provenance — the MUA dollar rule's formula switches from page-163's ungated `household_entitled_to_mandatory_utility_allowance` to page-165's `multiple_utility_allowance_entitlement`, which the same commit redefines as that entitlement AND `same_residence_utility_allowance_agreement_requirement_satisfied`. The pinned corpus text for us-sc/manual/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-165 states the clause verbatim ("Multiple households living in the same residence must agree on the type of utility allowance, either MUA, BUA or actual."), and pre-fix that condition existed in page-165 only as an orphan rule referenced by nothing, so it could not affect any dollar output — the encoding paid the $388 MUA to a shared-residence household that had not agreed. The companion test added in the same commit pins the meaning change (`sc_current_snap_standard_utility_allowance_state_value: 0` with `multiple_households_agree_on_utility_allowance_type_mua_bua_or_actual: false`), ruling out mechanical and test_only. This is a source-stated condition missing from the encoding that the fix adds, so unrepresented_clause fits better than untraceable_branch (nothing ungrounded was removed; the page-163 grounding for MUA entitlement remains valid) or polarity_or_logic (a conjunct was added, not inverted).
triage.verifier_notes: Scope caveat for the reviewer: within module 0 (page-159.yaml) only `sc_current_snap_standard_utility_allowance_state_value` has its own formula/import-target changed; the other two named rules (`..._limited_...`, `..._individual_...`) change only their import hashes (15aefb4d… → 9146cdfb…), and their meaning shifts transitively because page-165's `basic_utility_allowance_entitlement` and `household_entitled_to_telephone_only_standard` gain the same agreement conjunct in module index 1 of this commit. The candidate's rule_path (rules[sc_current_snap_standard_utility_allowance_state_value].versions[0].formula) is therefore the correct anchor. One genuine residual (why I hold at 0.85 rather than higher): the manual says households "must agree on the type" but does not state the consequence of non-agreement, so zeroing MUA/BUA/actual/telephone (fail-closed to $0) is the encoder's chosen semantics rather than text the source spells out — the missing-clause finding stands regardless, since pre-fix the clause had zero effect on any output, but a reviewer grading severity should note the fail-closed reading is an interpretation. Also note the first-reader quote is from a PR issue comment by MaxGhenis ("Repair round 2"), not a formal PR review; the commit subject "fix: require shared-residence utility agreement" and the round-1 comment's "orphaned shared-residence condition" finding corroborate it independently.
